reason: 'Sori discrete or confluent', 'androecium of discrete filaments' = like parts not united, the reading already used for 'distinct' and 'separate' (rules C177/C178).

target: new: conjunction of two values of one bearer (flattened PATO_0002254 + elliptic PATO_0000947, whose synonym is ellipsoid)
reason: Not a midpoint between two shapes but an ellipsoid body that is also flattened. Both qualities exist, so two values of one bearer are needed, not a new term.

target: new: conjunction of two values of one bearer (panicle-like FLOPO:0991198 + corymb-like PATO_0002455)
reason: A panicle with a flat-topped, corymbose outline: both values hold at once and both have terms.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum (qualitative_value_relation), as linear-lanceolate; oblong PATO_0000946 + oblanceolate PATO_0002330
reason: A shape between two existing values, the continuum already used for linear-lanceolate.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: Like 'similar' (C245), it needs the parts compared and the attribute (shape, size). Where 'leaves dimorphic' is meant, the existing rule for dimorphic (FLOPO:0991092) covers it.

label: unistratose
definition: An unstratified quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting of a single layer of cells. NOTE: Mainly bryophyte laminae and margins; the opposite, bistratose or multistratose, falls under PATO:0002068 stratified.
reason: A well-defined bryological quality. PATO unstratified only says 'not layered' and does not fix the thickness at one cell.
A faint red colour, treated like 'greenish': the colour value marked as approximate.
Angustate = narrowed (towards the base), the same reading as the rule for 'narrowed' (C172).
Diagonal branches and veins run at a slant to the axis. PATO_0002392 'diagonal to' is relational and needs a second term. 'Cells in diagonal rows' is an arrangement and fits less well.
'Evident' maps to conspicuous (C323), and 'obscure'/'indistinct' map to inconspicuous. 'Veins not evident' = not clearly visible.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum (qualitative_value_relation), as linear-lanceolate; linear PATO_0001199 + elliptic PATO_0000947
reason: A shape between two existing values.
Scanty hairs, pappus or gemmae = few and thinly spread. 'Scanty endosperm' is an amount and fits less well.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): margin of the bearer + glandular-pubescent (FLOPO:0991173)
reason: Minute gland-tipped hairs on the margin: the existing glandular hair value placed on the margin, rather than a new term. PATO has no plant 'ciliate'.
Every example is 'stipular spines'. PO has the part itself (EXACT synonym 'stipule spine'), so the word picks the bearer, not a quality.
The examples state a whitish colour of a surface ('often whitened at base'). Glaucous (PATO_0104277) would also claim a waxy coating that the word does not always mean.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md kind A (stage): PO dormant stages, e.g. bud dormancy stage PO_0025529, seed dormant stage PO_0025374, plant embryo dormant stage PO_0025377, sporophyte dormant stage PO_0007132
reason: Dormancy is a stage of development that PO already names, not a lasting quality. PATO has no plant 'dormant'.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum (qualitative_value_relation); obovate PATO_0001936 + orbicular PATO_0001934 marked approximate (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md)
reason: A shape between obovate and nearly round. Both have terms, and the 'sub-' is the approximate-value pattern.

label: interpetiolar
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being inserted on the stem between the petioles of two opposite leaves. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991000 axillary; typically stipules of Rubiaceae.
reason: A precise and common botanical position with no PATO or FLOPO term.

label: gynodioecious
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its belonging to a species whose individuals bear either only female flowers or only bisexual flowers. NOTE: Follows FLOPO:0991072 dioecious and FLOPO:0991094 andromonoecious.
reason: A standard breeding system that sits beside the existing FLOPO sex-distribution values. No term exists.
Unribbed = not ribbed, as 'unlobed' = not lobed (C239).

label: pseudolateral
definition: A positional quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its being terminal on the stem but appearing lateral because the lowest involucral bract continues the line of the stem beyond it. NOTE: Juncaceae, Cyperaceae.
reason: A defined term in rush and sedge floras. Annotating it as lateral (PATO_0001193) would be wrong.

label: whip-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long, slender and flexible, like a whip. NOTE: Flagellate branches and stems, the whip-like appendix of an Arisaema spadix, a rachis ending in a flagellum.
reason: A common shape word with no term. It is not PATO_0104351 filiform, which is thread-thin rather than long and whip-like.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md: continuum (qualitative_value_relation); lanceolate PATO_0001877 + subulate PATO_0001954
reason: A shape between two existing values. PATO_0002338 lanceolate-triangular shows such compounds get a term only when PATO already has one.
The examples mix swollen nodes, gnarled branches and lumpy rhizomes. PATO_0002427 knobbled (very small surface bumps) fits none of them well.

label: napiform
definition: A 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a turnip: broad and rounded above and abruptly narrowed below. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991077 turbinate.
reason: A standard shape for roots, tubers and Eriogonum involucres, with no PATO term.
Two-keeled, a count of keels. 'keeled → keel' is in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv, and the single-keel reading is keel-shaped (C221).
A calyx with its sepals joined = sepals connate, the same value as 'sepals united' (C171). The quality is carried by the sepals of the calyx.
A growth-form noun for a plant that creeps. 'Creeper or climber' is then two alternatives. Some Asian floras use 'creeper' for a climber, so this is not certain.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): awn (PO_0025349) + decreased length (PATO_0000574)
reason: The awn is present and short: a quality of the awn of the lemma or bract, not a quality of the bearer itself.

label: stipule-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a stipule. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002457 leaf-like.
reason: Follows bract-like and sepal-like. No 'like a stipule' term exists.
